note:
1.4.1 for the wagmi tier. This tier carries 1.3.1, so a claw here crosses two
releases in one apply and 1.4.0 is the skipped one. The run back-fills one
changelog entry for 1.4.0 below 1.4.1's own. Class fix. Disruption quiet:
neither core floor moves, codex stays at 0.147.0 and claude at 2.1.227.

1.4.0's landing section has to be read, because a claw crossing it never meets
it through the rail. It asks for two things and neither one fails a run. Put
this claw's channel webhook into its vault, or the memory alarm and the stall
report find what they find and nothing leaves the box. And enrol this claw's
dead-man check, which is one command on the operator's side and one on the
claw. Until both halves are done the five-minute beat skips the ping in
silence.

The box half, measured on wagmi-claw at 16:24 UTC on 2026-09-02 before this
pointer was written. claw-members holds two people. Both hold a persistent core
at or above the floor, at 2.1.252 and 2.1.227, and the per-task core sits at
its floor with its companion host present. So no member reads as below a floor
and this claw's own classifier will not defer the release to the quiet window.
A claw on this channel measures itself the same way before it rides: one read
of the members group, and one look at each member's launcher.

Wide mode is on here, and this is the first release a wide-mode claw can take.
1.4.0's claw-admin door phase proved its scope by asking what a member may run,
and under wide mode the honest answer is everything, so three checks failed and
the apply stopped. 1.4.1 reads the door file itself, which is where the scope
is written, and says out loud that no live refusal is possible on a claw whose
members hold passwordless root by its own ruling. A claw with wide mode off
still gets the live refusal pair.

The other change to riding one is the health line. It is now
scripts/unit-health.sh and it has two halves: nothing failed, and nothing in
activating carrying a restart count. An empty systemctl --failed on its own is
no longer the reading. A unit with Restart= never settles into failed, so the
old line called a looping box healthy.

The wake rail's per-account unit no longer fails when that account has nobody
signed in. It idles, says so once, and delivers when a session opens. Before
this release that state exited the unit, systemd restarted it every ten
seconds, and the failed unit took a whole apply down on this claw on
2026-09-02. Both members here are signed in right now, so this claw exercises
the ordinary ready path rather than the idle one.

wagmi-claw already runs most of 1.4.0's payload, left by that failed apply
while its record stayed at 1.3.1. This apply converges the rest and advances
the record. Four copies on the box are older than what this release ships and
each one is replaced by digest and named in the run's own output rather than in
silence: the notifier, the wake rail program, the heartbeat door and the
updater itself.

The updater fix in a release lands one release late, because the apply is
performed by the updater the claw already has. So this apply prints no
end-of-run health line, and the reading arrives from the next update. Running
scripts/unit-health.sh by hand works today.

The operator runbook lands at /opt/commonclaw/doc/operator-runbook.md on every
claw that takes this release.
